questions.question: How many grapes are shown in the picture?
questions.explain: Each picture stands for one grape. Count the grape pictures to get 7, and make sure you read the grape row, not the apple row.

questions.question: How many blue crayons are in the picture?
questions.explain: One picture means one crayon, so count the blue pictures to get 6. Doubling the count would be wrong because each picture is just one.

questions.question: How many books did Sam read on Monday?
questions.explain: Find the Mon row and count the pictures to get 3. The Tue row has 5, so be careful to read the right one.

questions.question: How many cats are in the picture?
questions.explain: One cat picture means one cat, so count them to get 6. Saying 12 would mean each picture is two cats, which is not true.

questions.question: Mia is picking fruit for a bake sale. She needs to know how many pears are ready. How many pears does the picture show?
questions.explain: Find the pear row and count the pictures to get 4. The apple row has 7, so be sure you read the right row.

questions.question: Liam joins one after-school club. The picture shows how many kids chose each club. How many kids chose soccer?
questions.explain: Each soccer picture is one kid, so count them to get 5. Doubling to 10 would mean each picture is two kids, which is not right.

questions.question: A shop counts the jelly pots by flavour. How many cherry jelly pots are in the picture?
questions.explain: Each cherry picture is one pot, so count them to get 9. The strawberry row has 6, so read the right row.

questions.question: A picture graph shows fish in two ponds. Pond A has 8 fish pictures, and there are 12 in both ponds. How many fish pictures are in Pond B?
questions.explain: There are 12 pictures in all and 8 are in Pond A, so take 8 away from 12 to get 4. Each picture is just one fish.

questions.question: Ava wants to give away all her moon stickers. The picture shows her stickers. How many moon stickers does she give away?
questions.explain: Find the moon row and count the pictures to get 2. The stars row has 7, so be careful to read the right one.

questions.question: A picture graph shows shoes in a small shop. The shop has 9 red shoe pictures, and 14 shoe pictures in all. How many blue shoe pictures are there?
questions.explain: There are 14 pictures in all and 9 are red, so take 9 away from 14 to get 5 blue pictures. Each picture is one shoe.

questions.question: Leo says, 'There are 12 dogs in the picture.' What did Leo do wrong?
options: He added the dogs and cats up.
He read the cat row by mistake.
He counted each picture as two.
He missed one picture when counting.
questions.explain: The picture has 6 dog pictures, and each picture is one dog. Leo doubled the count, as if each picture were two dogs.

questions.question: A market stall sells muffins. The picture shows the muffins left. How many blueberry muffins are left?
questions.explain: Find the Blueberry row and count its pictures one at a time: 7. One picture stands for 1 muffin, so 7 pictures is 7 muffins, not 14.

visual.caption: Muffins left at the market stall

questions.question: Eli helps in the school garden. The picture shows the plants growing there. How many tomato plants are there?
questions.explain: Stay on the Tomato row and count each plant picture: 5. Each picture is 1 plant, so do not double it, and do not slide down to the Bean row.

questions.question: Nina counts birds at the park. The picture shows the birds she saw. How many ducks did she see?
questions.explain: Put your finger on the Duck row and count the bird pictures: 4. One picture means 1 duck, so 4 pictures is 4 ducks.

visual.caption: Birds Nina saw at the park

questions.question: Ava brings one carrot for each rabbit. The picture shows the class pets. How many carrots does Ava bring?
questions.explain: Count the pictures in the Rabbit row: 8 rabbits, so 8 carrots. Each picture stands for 1 rabbit, so counting each one as 2 gives too many.
